goals.label: Food aid is used as currency or traded within the camp
Accountability and documentation of distribution for donors
Burdensome assessments and procedures are imposed on the camp
Camp guard and militia structures control food distribution and camp operations
Camp receives a steady, ongoing food supply
Camp stays stable without riots, violence or perimeter breach
Commander controls the camp narrative and ties with local partners like MASHA
Commander's authority and standing with guards and militia
FWB controls and oversees food distribution
FWB neutrality, with aid not supporting armed guards
FWB staff and partners are safe from threats or violence
FWB staff have access and freedom of movement in the camp
FWB's reputation, visibility and donor funding
Food aid is diverted or skimmed by guards, militia or camp authorities
Food is distributed equally to all refugee groups
Guards and their families are fed and compensated
Host town's economy and local actors are prioritised
Refugees receive enough food to meet nutritional needs
Refugees stay contained in the camp and away from the capital
Refugees' needs and views are heard
Reliable nutritional needs data from independent assessments
Senior Militia Leader's trust and expectations are maintained

redLines.label: Allow FWB representatives and chosen assistants to manage food disbursement

assumptions: Commitments are binding and additive.
Goals and goal-action links were each extracted 3 times by a model; only those found in a majority of runs are kept.
Actions are chosen to bring about as much goal value as possible, within the solver's size limit.
Our values are the median of stances elicited from our role card.
The opponent column is the expected value of an elicited stance distribution (shared documents only); each opponent reading is one draw from it, independently per goal.
Stance labels map to numbers by a fixed scale (game.stance_values), not a measured utility.

Red lines and must-haves come from our role card, each with a verbatim quote. No plan may include a red-line action, leave out a must-have, or pass through a state worth less to us than our BATNA (the bottom line).
